name: The Ascent
design_intent:
THE ASCENT — the vertical DUAL-BLAST level (v1_level_circuit.md §L-7, the final core-circuit build). A four-tier tower climbed up a walled SHAFT toward a deliberately LOW sky lid, over a bottom void. Kill identity = a DUAL VERTICAL blast: the ONLY two ways to die are UP through the low top bound or DOWN into the bottom void. The LEFT and RIGHT sides are NON-lethal BUMPER walls (drop_chamber's sanctioned technique, restitution 0.86) — a sideways knock RICOCHETS back into the kill channel instead of a cheap side ring-out, so all lethality is vertical. Kill-shape class = dual_blast; QA uses AS1 per docs/specs/v2a_kill_shape_void_floor_addendum.md §3 — top kills >=20% AND bottom/void present AND combined off-screen >=90% — NOT the generic 'top rare' expectation of v2 §1d (this is the sanctioned exception, via a per-level bounds.top override, not a global bounds_top_margin change).

TOP-BOUND OVERRIDE (the level's whole identity): the explicit "bounds" block sets top=-700, only 480px above the top DECK (top=-220), FAR lower than the derived bounds_top_margin=2650 would give. This is a sanctioned per-level JSON bounds override (LevelLoader uses the explicit bounds block when present; Tuning 'Level-relative bounds'). Wiring CONFIRMED in-engine: PartyMatch rings out on ANY bound crossing (COMBAT tick: `not bounds.has_point(pos) -> kill(ring_out)`), and _classify_blast_edge returns "top" for a top crossing — a living player placed above y=-700 is outside bounds, classifies "top", and is killed by the ring-out tick (verified). The low bounds.top is a LETHAL top blast, not a soft camera bound. There is NO ceiling bumper (unlike drop_chamber) — the top is OPEN and LETHAL. NO lethality/feel constant touched — geometry + the per-level bounds override + bumper walls only (fence per v1_level_circuit.md §6).

DUAL-BLAST TUNING (in-engine QA drove this): v1 (open narrow arena, sides ~480px, lid 780px) -> ~4.5% top / ~61% side; v2 (open wide arena, lid 520px) -> ~0% top / ~48% side — in BOTH, combat gravitated DOWN to the base and sideways knocks bled out the OPEN sides, so upward launches never reached the lid. v3 fix (GEOMETRY only): (a) enclose the sides with NON-lethal BUMPER walls so a sideways knock ricochets back into the vertical kill channel instead of a cheap side kill — now the ONLY exits are UP (lid) and DOWN (void); (b) make the TOP tier a WIDE central DECK (the main stage) directly under a LOW lid so the sustained combat happens right beneath the ceiling — an upward smash on the deck rings the victim out the TOP; (c) keep the lower climb tiers small over the void so falls/low fights resolve DOWN into the void. The deck is a TRAMPOLINE (apex 270): a routine deck bounce (270 -> y-490) and even a boost-bounce supercharged one (270*1.4=378 -> y-598) stay INSIDE the -700 lid (AS2 second half safe, >=100px margin), while a committed upward smash/super rings out the top (AS2 first half). No lethality/feel constant touched.

SIGNATURE / DISTINCT FROM the nine prior shipped levels: islands_void horizontal archipelago; the_spine one thin ridge; twin_chasms two-void split; the_cliff asymmetric mesa+scatter; atoll radial ring; bumper_gauntlet interior-pinball; grassy_expanse central pit. SPIRES is the other vertical level but has NO lid (top bound -2610, top kills rare). DROP_CHAMBER is the other bumper-walled level but is enclosed on THREE sides (bumper ceiling too) with a SINGLE exit — the bottom hole (down-only kills). THE ASCENT is the only level with TWO vertical lethal exits: a lethal LOW LID on top AND a full void on the bottom, with bumper walls on the sides only — you climb the shaft and can be smashed to death UP or DOWN. Vertical-dual-blast (up-OR-down, walled channel) belongs to no other level.

GEOMETRY (a walled vertical SHAFT: inner faces x0..x1600; four tiers zigzag up to a WIDE top deck under a LOW lid, over ONE bottom void): T1 base trampoline x540..1060 top1400 (center 800, over the void) / T2 spring x870..1330 top860 (center 1100) / T3 spring x270..730 top320 (center 500) / T_DECK trampoline x250..1350 top-220 (center 800, WIDE main stage under the lid). LEFT + RIGHT vertical BUMPER walls (x-100..0 inner face x0 / x1600..1700 inner face x1600, y-700..1620) seal the shaft sides NON-lethally. ONE full-shaft-width bottom void (rim y1560, a dark bottomless chasm just under the base) runs the whole inner width. Bounds left-500/right2100 sit OUTSIDE the bumper walls as pure failsafes (the walls stop any side ring-out first, so sides are non-lethal by construction); bottom y2200 leaves a 672px recovery sky under the base; TOP y-700 is the LOW LETHAL LID (480px above the deck).

MOVEMENT-TOOL-PER-GAP ANALYSIS (Tuning.gd: trampoline apex 270px / spring apex 480 (the highest); air_drift_max 340px/s, gravity 1600 => zero-boost horizontal reach ~395px off a trampoline / ~527px off a spring (the MAX possible drift); normal_boost_max 760px/s + normal_boost_accel 4600 (> gravity 1600 => sustained climb); super_boost_impulse_full 2800 => a straight-up self-super rises 2800^2/(2*1600) = 2450px). This level's required traversal is entirely VERTICAL CLIMBS (Rule B), each a 540px vertical rise (> the 480 spring apex, the max bounce) with a horizontal offset (diagonal arc, not a straight column):
- CLIMB T1->T2: 540px UP (1400->860) AND 300px horizontal (center 800->1100). 540 > 480 (spring apex) and >> 270 (trampoline). A trampoline bounce off T1 reaches only y1130 — 270px short of T2. JETPACK CLIMB REQUIRED (diagonal boost arc); an under-shot climb drops into the void. Verb: FLY. (Rule B.)
- CLIMB T2->T3: 540px UP (860->320) AND 600px horizontal (1100->500). > 480 spring apex; a spring bounce off T2 reaches only y380 — 60px short of T3 AND 600px sideways. JETPACK CLIMB REQUIRED. Verb: FLY.
- CLIMB T3->DECK: 540px UP (320->-220) to the wide top deck. > 480 spring apex (spring off T3 reaches y-160, 60px short). JETPACK CLIMB REQUIRED; a mis-aimed climb drops back down the shaft toward the void. Verb: FLY (+ SUPER earns the deck fast). (Rule B/C.)
- Because EVERY tier-to-tier rise (540px) exceeds the 480px spring apex (the highest bounce in the game), zero-boost from any tier reaches NO tier above it — you climb the shaft ONLY on the jetpack (AS3, >=9/10 zero-boost fails). There is no same-height horizontal crossing and no bounce route up; a bumper wall is a REFLECTOR, never a climbing aid (it only redirects an airborne body horizontally, it does not lift you the 540px to the next tier). Vertical distance is the entire level, not scenery.
- RECOVER after being knocked off a tier: the drop from the base tier's bottom (1528) to the bottom blast line (2200) is 672px of open sky over the void (>= 650, Rule D); knocked off the deck you fall PAST the lower tiers with far more sky, so a fuelled player can boost to catch a lower tier or arc back (recovery gamble, vertical flavour), while a near-brink dead-on down-smash or a starved/damaged victim falls into the void forever. A sideways knock RICOCHETS off a bumper wall back into play (non-lethal) — recovery is always vertical. Verb: FLY. (Rule D.)

THE LETHAL LID (dual-blast, the identity — top clearance = 480px above the deck top -220 => bounds.top -700; the deck is a TRAMPOLINE): a routine deck bounce rises 270px to y-490, staying 210px INSIDE the lid (does NOT ring out — AS2 second half); even a boost-bounce supercharged bounce (supercharge_bounce_mult 1.4 => 378px) reaches y-598, still 102px inside; the spring mid-tiers (T2/T3) bounce far below the lid. But a full super fired straight up rises 2450px (exits by ~1730px) and a committed upward smash on the deck (a ~480px+ up-launch, routinely produced by a super or a chained/wounded smash which caps near max_speed 3000 => ~2812px rise) rings the victim out the TOP — so the lid punishes COMMITTED upward launches while normal bouncing is safe (AS2). Combat concentrates on the wide deck directly under the lid, so an up-angled smash there rings the victim out the TOP; a knock off the deck edge or a lower-tier fight drops the victim DOWN into the void; the bumper walls remove the sideways escape — the two VERTICAL blasts define every death. VOID READS AS DEATH via the pit_void_rendering treatment (dark cool bottomless gradient + receding dirt canyon walls at the base cliffs + under-lip AO + matte hazard-red rim/chevrons along y1560 + falling motes) so the base chasm is unmistakably lethal; the low top is a dark lid you climb toward.

SUCCESS CRITERIA (dual_blast class, §L-7): AS1 — >=12 stages: TOP blast kills >=20% of credited kills (the ONE level where top is common) AND bottom/void kills present AND combined off-screen >=90%. AS2 — top override intentional, not a bug: a full super fired straight up from the deck rings out the top >=7/10; a routine deck bounce does NOT exit (< 1/10). AS3 — flight-required: zero-boost cannot climb tier-to-tier (bounce apex < the 540px climb) >=9/10. Uncredited self-falls reported RELATIVE to the flagship (~44% under all-bot melee is normal for void levels).
